arxiv-1911-00289.title: Does Adam optimizer keep close to the optimal point?
arxiv-1911-00289.creator: Kiwook Bae, Heechang Ryu, Hayong Shin
arxiv-1911-00289.description: Abstract The adaptive optimizer for training neural networks has continually evolved to overcome the limitations of the previously proposed adaptive methods. Recent studies have found the rare counterexamples that Adam cannot converge to the optimal point. Those counterexamples reveal the distortion of Adam due to a small second momentum from a small gradient.

arxiv-2203-14737.title: Time spent in a ball by a critical branching random walk
arxiv-2203-14737.creator: Amine Asselah, Bruno Schapira
arxiv-2203-14737.description: Abstract We study a critical branching random walk on ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} . We focus on the tail of the time spent in a ball, and our study, in dimension four and higher, sheds new light on the recent result of Angel, Hutchcroft and Jarai [ AHJ21 ] , in particular on the special features of the critical dimension four.

arxiv-2207-05946.title: Distribution Theoretic Semantics for Non-Smooth Differentiable Programming CCS: Software and its engineering General programming languages CCS: Social and professional topics History of programming languages
arxiv-2207-05946.creator: Pedro H. Azevedo de Amorim, Christopher Lam
arxiv-2207-05946.description: Abstract . With the wide spread of deep learning and gradient descent inspired optimization algorithms, differentiable programming has gained traction. Nowadays it has found applications in many different areas as well, such as scientific computing, robotics, computer graphics and others. One of its notoriously difficult problems consists in interpreting programs that are not differentiable everywhere.

arxiv-2209-01939.title: Incremental Permutation Feature Importance (iPFI): Towards Online Explanations on Data Streams
arxiv-2209-01939.creator: Fabian Fumagalli, Maximilian Muschalik, Eyke Hüllermeier, Barbara Hammer
arxiv-2209-01939.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fabian Fumagalli, Maximilian Muschalik, Eyke Hüllermeier, Barbara Hammer. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has mainly focused on static learning scenarios so far. We are interested in dynamic scenarios where data is sampled progressively, and learning is done in an incremental rather than a batch mode. We seek efficient incremental algorithms for computing feature importance (FI) measures, specifically, an incremental FI measure based on feature marginalization of absent features similar to permutation feature importance (PFI).

arxiv-2209-08745.title: Importance Tempering: Group Robustness for Overparameterized Models
arxiv-2209-08745.creator: Yiping Lu, Wenlong Ji, Zachary Izzo, Lexing Ying
arxiv-2209-08745.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yiping Lu, Wenlong Ji, Zachary Izzo, Lexing Ying. Although overparameterized models have shown their success on many machine learning tasks, the accuracy could drop on the testing distribution that is different from the training one. This accuracy drop still limits applying machine learning in the wild. At the same time, importance weighting, a traditional technique to handle distribution shifts, has been demonstrated to have less or even no effect on overparameterized models both empirically and theoretically.

arxiv-2210-11235.title: Application of Explainable Machine Learning in Detecting and Classifying Ransomware Families Based on API Call Analysis Thanks: This work is funded by NetApp.
arxiv-2210-11235.creator: Rawshan Ara Mowri, Madhuri Siddula, Kaushik Roy
arxiv-2210-11235.description: Abstract Ransomware has appeared as one of the major global threats in recent days. The alarming increasing rate of ransomware attacks and new ransomware variants intrigue the researchers to constantly examine the distinguishing traits of ransomware and refine their detection strategies.

arxiv-2212-04785.title: Exact solution of the boundary-dissipated transverse field Ising model: Structure of Liouvillian spectrum and dynamical duality
arxiv-2212-04785.creator: Zhen-Yu Zheng, Xueliang Wang, Shu Chen
arxiv-2212-04785.description: Abstract We study the boundary-dissipated transverse field Ising model described by a Lindblad Master equation and exactly solve its Liouvillian spectrum in the whole parameter space. By mapping the Liouvillian into a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with imaginary boundary potentials under a parity constraint, we solve the rapidity spectrum analytically and thus construct the Liouvillian spectrum strictly with a parity constraint condition.

arxiv-2312-12336.title: Optical Feedback Loop in Paraxial Fluids of Light: A Gate to New Phenomena in Analogue Physical Simulations
arxiv-2312-12336.creator: Tiago D. Ferreira, Ariel Guerreiro, Nuno A. Silva
arxiv-2312-12336.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tiago D. Ferreira, Ariel Guerreiro, Nuno A. Silva. Easily accessible through tabletop experiments based on laser propagation inside nonlinear optical media, Paraxial Fluids of Light are emerging as promising platforms for the simulation and exploration of quantum-like phenomena. In particular, the analogy builds on a formal equivalence between the governing model for a Bose-Einstein Condensate under the mean-field approximation and the model of laser propagation under the paraxial approximation.

arxiv-2404-15898.title: Quantum metrology in a driven-dissipation down-conversion system beyond the parametric approximation
arxiv-2404-15898.creator: Dong Xie, Chunling Xu
arxiv-2404-15898.description: Abstract We investigate quantum metrology in a degenerate down-conversion system composed of a pump mode and two degenerate signal modes. In the conventional parametric approximation, the pump mode is assumed to be constant, not a quantum operator. We obtain the measurement precision of the coupling strength between the pump mode and two degenerate signal modes beyond the parametric approximation.

arxiv-2406-07316.title: Multimessenger constraints for electrophilic feebly interacting particles from supernovae
arxiv-2406-07316.creator: Pedro De la Torre Luque 1,2,, Shyam Balaji 3,4, Pierluca Carenza 5
arxiv-2406-07316.description: Abstract Several extensions of the Standard Model predict the existence of sub-GeV particles that can be copiously produced in the cores of supernovae. A broad family of these particles are dubbed feebly interacting particles (FIPs), which can have masses of up to a few hundreds of MeV.

arxiv-2501-09943.title: Indigenous Languages Spoken in Argentina: A Survey of NLP and Speech Resources
arxiv-2501-09943.creator: Belu Ticona, Fernando Carranza, Viviana Cotik
arxiv-2501-09943.description: Abstract Argentina has a large yet little-known Indigenous linguistic diversity, encompassing at least 40 different languages. The majority of these languages are at risk of disappearing, resulting in a significant loss of world heritage and cultural knowledge. Currently, unified information on speakers and computational tools is lacking for these languages.

arxiv-2503-12570.title: Exceptional-point-controlled mode interaction in three-dimensional microcavities represented by generalized Husimi functions
arxiv-2503-12570.creator: Tom Simon Rodemund, Shilong Li, Síle Nic Chormaic, Martina Hentschel
arxiv-2503-12570.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tom Simon Rodemund, Shilong Li, Síle Nic Chormaic, Martina Hentschel. Non-Hermitian photonics has attracted significant interest and influences several key areas such as optical metamaterials, laser physics, and nonlinear optics. While non-Hermitian effects have been widely addressed in two-dimensional systems, we focus on realistic three-dimensional devices. To this end we generalize established phase space methods from mesoscopic optics and introduce Husimi functions for three-dimensional systems that deepen the insight and access to the mode morphology and their dynamics.

arxiv-2511-12799.title: Verified Implementation of GRAPE Pulse Optimization for Quantum Gates with Hardware-Representative Noise Models
arxiv-2511-12799.creator: Rylan Malarchick
arxiv-2511-12799.description: Abstract Gate fidelity in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) computers remains the primary bottleneck limiting practical quantum computation, constrained by decoherence and control noise. Note: This work presents results from closed quantum system optimization (unitary evolution without decoherence during the optimization process). The reported 99.

pmc-10740075.creator: Enhan Zhang, Yuan Zhao, Zhongyang Ren, Linfan Shi, Wuyin Weng
pmc-10740075.description: Highlights•The added W/O emulsion weakened the dense surimi gel network.•The oil droplets were evenly dispersed in gel network structure with O/W emulsion.•The breaking force of surimi gels was decreased by adding W/O emulsion.•The breaking force of surimi gels was not affected by adding of O/W emulsion.

pmc-11392125.title: The role of coagulopathy and subdural hematoma thickness at admission in predicting the prognoses of patients with severe traumatic brain injury: a multicenter retrospective cohort study from China
pmc-11392125.creator: Li Chen, Shaohuai Xia, Yinghong Lin, Yuhui Chen, Liang Xian, Yang Yang, Xianshen Qiu, Limei Xu, Zhu Xingshu, Dujuan Chen, Xuewei Xia, Yi Zuo, Shousen Wang
pmc-11392125.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background:Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is one of the diseases with high disability and mortality worldwide. Recent studies have shown that TBI-related factors may change the complex balance between bleeding and thrombosis, leading to coagulation disorders.

pmc-11416160.title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury in Saudi Arabia: A Systematic Review
pmc-11416160.creator: Albaraa M Almallah, Ghaida A Albattah, Asmaa A Altarqi, Amr A Al Sattouf, Khalid M Alameer, Dalal M Hamithi, Ryan D Alghamdi, Mohmmed S AlShammri, Bandar M Abuageelah, Abdulhadi Y Algahtani
pmc-11416160.description: Traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI) is a severe condition with high mortality and disability rates. Understanding the regional TSCI epidemiology may facilitate the development of targeted preventive initiatives and the optimization of resource allocation. The primary goal of this systematic review was to gather and analyze the existing literature on the frequency and characteristics of TSCI in Saudi Arabia.

pmc-11523772.title: A retrospective cohort study on a novel marker to predict the severity and prognosis of acute cerebral venous thrombosis: D-dimer to fibrinogen ratio
pmc-11523772.creator: Duo Lan, Mengqi Wang, Xiaoming Zhang, Xiangqian Huang, Naiqi Liu, Xiangyu Ren, Kun Fang, Da Zhou, Ran Meng
pmc-11523772.description: Background and aimThe D-dimer to fibrinogen ratio (DFR) represents an emerging and significant clinical biomarker. However, its correlation with cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) remains underexplored. This retrospective cohort study aims to elucidate the association between DFR values and the severity and prognosis of CVT.

pmc-11666536.title: Attendance rate and perceived relevance related to type, content, and delivery of current rehabilitation programmes after surgical resection for non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-11666536.creator: Mette Kaasgaard, Uffe Bodtger, Anders Løkke, Erik Jakobsen, Ole Hilberg
pmc-11666536.description: BackgroundSurgical resection is the preferred treatment for localised non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Rehabilitation is central in the management of the associated impaired quality of life, high symptom burden, deconditioning, and social-existential vulnerability. Yet, optimal content and delivery of rehabilitation are not yet defined.

pmc-12440506.title: A real-world data analysis of Ozanimod in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database
pmc-12440506.creator: Qinhui Tang, Xiaowei Tang, Xinyue Hu, Wenmeng Yin, Lian Luo, Yantong Li, Xiaolin Zhong
pmc-12440506.description: Ozanimod was approved in the United States in March 2020 for the treatment of relapsing multiple sclerosis and subsequently in 2021 for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. However, there is limited information available on the adverse drug events associated with its use. The main objective of this study was to explore the safety of Ozanimod after its market launch.

pmc-12766114.title: Endoscopic Retroperitoneal Debridement Combined with Posterior Percutaneous Pedicle Screw Fixation for Lumbar Infectious Spondylodiscitis: A Retrospective Study and Preliminary Results
pmc-12766114.creator: Yongrui Yang, Wenkai Ruan, Jianlong Li, Rongpan Dang, Huigang An, Wentao Zhao, Liang Xu, Hongdong Tan
pmc-12766114.description: BackgroundLumbar infectious spondylodiscitis is a severe spinal condition traditionally managed with antibiotics, though some patients require surgical intervention. The heterogeneity in infection sites, causative pathogens, and clinical presentations leads to significant variability in surgical approaches, and optimal surgical strategies remain controversial.

pmc-13074733.title: Multifunctional Bioactivity of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Extracellular Vesicle in Hair Follicle-Related Cellular Models
pmc-13074733.creator: Hannah S. Park, Eunji Shin, Sehyun Shin
pmc-13074733.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from microbial sources, including beer yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), have recently attracted increasing attention as bioactive nanostructures with potential biomedical and cosmetic applications. In this study, EVs were isolated from Saccharomyces cerevisiae (beer yeast) using an electrokinetic ion-binding filtration system, followed by tangential flow filtration (TFF)-based buffer exchange.

pmc-13429212.title: Current Evidence, Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions of Rotator Cuff Failure: A Systematic Review
pmc-13429212.creator: Maithili V Potdar, Sandeep Shinde, Akshaya V Joshi, Sanjaykumar Patil
pmc-13429212.description: Rotator cuff tears (RTs) are among the most prevalent musculoskeletal conditions worldwide, imposing substantial burdens of chronic pain, functional limitation, and socioeconomic cost. The underlying pathophysiology is multifactorial, encompassing progressive mechanical attrition, tendon degeneration, and irreversible biological deterioration, including muscle atrophy, fatty infiltration, and altered glenohumeral kinematics that may ultimately culminate in cuff tear arthropathy.
